title: Working with others to compete

draft.title: Working with others to compete
card: A business does not have to build its competitive advantage alone. It can work with other businesses in its industry, with government, and with training providers.
businesses in the same industry can pool money to promote their product together, such as a campaign for Australian beef overseas. Each business pays only part of the cost.
government agencies can help businesses find overseas buyers and learn how to export. This can lower the cost and risk of selling abroad.
training workers gives a business staff with the skills to make better products or give better service. This can help it compete with rivals.
draft.remember: Working with others can help a business compete by sharing costs, getting support and building skills.

a.q: Five wine makers in the Barossa Valley each put money into one joint advertising campaign overseas. What is the main benefit to each wine maker?
opts: Each pays only a share of the promotion cost
Each gets free export help from government
Each gets staff who have been trained for free
Each sells the same wine under one brand name
a.why: Pooling money means the cost of the campaign is split, so each wine maker pays only part of it. Government help is tempting, but the scenario only describes businesses working together.
a.clue: Think about who pays for the advertising.

b.q: Jess runs a small furniture business in Hobart and wants to sell to buyers overseas, but has never exported. Which step is an example of working with others to compete?
opts: Asking a government agency for help with exporting
Cutting her prices below those of every rival
Making her own furniture designs look different
Using social media to post photos of her work
b.why: Government agencies can help businesses find overseas buyers and learn how to export, so asking one for help is working with others. Posting photos and changing designs are things Jess does alone, so they are not working with others.
b.clue: Which step involves someone outside her business?

a.best: Each pays only a share of the promotion cost

b.best: Asking a government agency for help with exporting
